newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish MPs vote against Ciller corruption probe.
newsitem.headline: Turkish MPs vote against Ciller corruption probe.

text.p: The Turkish parliament on Wednesday decided against setting up an inquiry into Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller that could have sent her to the Supreme Court on corruption charges.

Deputy parliament speaker Uluc Gurkan told the house that deputies rejected by 269 votes to 259 an opposition proposal to probe allegations that Ciller was involved in corruption at the state-owned Turban hotel and tourism company.
The vote would have caused a rift in the government if coalition partner Islamist Welfare Party MPs had swayed it against Ciller.
The executive body of parliament announced earlier on Wednesday that the vote was to be repeated after investigation of challenges against the validity of last month's initial vote.
After the first vote the opposition said two or three government MPs were counted as having voted for Ciller despite not being in attendance at the ballot.

The accusations over Turban date back to Ciller's three years as Turkey's first woman prime minister from 1993. They include claims that Ciller blocked the prosecution of Turban's former boss, now an MP in her True Path Party (DYP), on corruption charges.
The main opposition Motherland Party also said Ciller used Turban's hotel and yacht marina facilities for personal purposes.

Ciller has already been cleared of corruption charges relating to state-owned car manufacturer TOFAS and the TEDAS state-run electricity company. A parliament commission has also voted against an investigation of her substantial personal wealth.
Wednesday's vote followed the filing of two censure motions by Turkey's major leftist parties against Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition government with Ciller's DYP.
The left-wing parties described their motions as a bid to safeguard the country's secular system against the emerging radicalism of some Islamists.
Under parliamentary rules, debate and vote on the censure motions must be held 16-23 days from the date of filing. Passage would bring an end to the seven-month-old coalition.
